p: why hast thou cast us off: The Church of God is oppressed by the tyranny, either of the Babylonians or of Antiochus, and prays to God by whose hand the yoke was laid on them for their sins.
rod of thine inheritance: Which inheritance you have measured out for yourself as with a line or rod.
set up their ensigns for signs: They have destroyed your true religion, and spread their banners in sign of defiance.
lifted up axes upon the thick: He commends the temple for the costly matter, the excellent workmanship and beauty of it, which nonetheless the enemies destroyed.
hearts: They encouraged one another to cruelty, that not only God's people might be destroyed, but also his religion utterly in all places suppressed.
how long: They lamented that they had no prophet among them to show them how long their misery would last.
pluck it out of thy bosom: They join their deliverance with God's glory and power, knowing that the punishment of the enemy would be their deliverance.
in the midst of the earth: Meaning in the sight of all the world.
dragons in the waters: That is, Pharaoh's army.
leviathan in pieces: Which was a great monster of the sea, or whale, meaning Pharaoh.
meat to the people inhabiting the: His destruction rejoiced them as meat refreshes the body.
day is thine: Seeing that God by his providence governs and disposes all things, he gathers that he will take care chiefly for his children.
turtledove unto the multitude of the: He means the Church of God, which is exposed as a prey to the wicked.
the dark places of the earth: That is, all places where your word does not shine, there reigns tyranny and ambition.
own cause: He shows that God cannot permit his Church to be oppressed unless he looses his own right.
